issues.description: Error-type membership encoded as a tuple with a duplicate string instead of a value (set/map of known errors)
issues.detail: The error branch uses a tuple of string literals with 'transcriber_error' listed twice. That duplication is not a typo so much as a symptom: the set of known error message_types is a value about the world (a fact: 'these are the error kinds ElevenLabs sends'), and it has been complected with the control-flow branch that handles it. Pull the set out as a module-level frozenset (or a dict mapping message_type -> human label) so the data is one thing, the dispatch is another, and duplicates become impossible by construction.

issues.description: Error dispatch still complects message-type, log message, and outgoing error frame in one ad-hoc branch
issues.detail: The previous code at least named auth_error and quota_exceeded with distinct human prefixes ('Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:'). The new code collapses everything to 'Error: <error>' and silently drops the per-type logger.error call that existed before. The right decomposition is data, not branches: a table {message_type: (log_prefix, frame_prefix)} consulted by a small handler. That separates the fact (what kinds exist, what they're called) from the behavior (log + push frame), and restores the lost per-type context without adding a branch per error.

issues.description: Inlining _process_messages into _receive_messages removes the only seam where 'connection closed' was observable as a distinct event
issues.detail: Before, there were two concerns separated by two methods: _process_messages handled per-message parsing errors; _receive_messages handled the lifecycle event of the async-for terminating (logged as 'WebSocket connection closed'). Merging them fixes the infinite-loop bug but also discards that lifecycle log, complecting 'a message failed to parse' with 'the stream ended'. Keep the two concerns separate: let _receive_messages drive the async-for and log a single 'stream ended, will reconnect' at the end, while per-message try/except stays a pure parse-and-dispatch step. The bug was the broad try/except wrapping the loop, not the existence of the inner method.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception' inside per-message loop still swallows everything, including programmer errors
issues.detail: The inner loop catches JSONDecodeError specifically (good) and then catches Exception (less good). That hides bugs in _process_response (KeyError, attribute errors on malformed data, etc.) behind a single logger.error and continues. A value-oriented version would validate the parsed dict shape once (message_type present, known type) and let unexpected exceptions propagate or be reported as a distinct error frame. As written, 'error processing message' is doing two jobs: 'their payload was weird' and 'our code has a bug'.

issues.description: Changelog file missing trailing newline; minor but a place-oriented artifact worth fixing
issues.detail: changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline ('\ No newline at end of file'). Tiny, but these markdown fragments are values that get concatenated by tooling; a missing newline is exactly the kind of incidental complexity that bites at integration time. Add the newline.

review.summary: The diff correctly identifies a real bug (the outer try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing the websocket-closed exception and the outer reconnect loop was spinning) and the fix direction is right: stop catching at the wrong altitude. But the implementation conflates two cleanups and trades one piece of incidental complexity for another. The expanded error handler is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: a long tuple of string literals (with 'transcriber_error' duplicated) inlined into a branch, when the underlying fact is just 'here is the set of error message_types and how each should be surfaced' — that is data, and it wants to live as data. The collapse of _process_messages into _receive_messages fixes the loop but also loses the distinct 'connection closed' log, complecting parse-failure with stream-end. The question that should have been asked first: what are the values here — the set of known error kinds, the parse result, the lifecycle event — and which of them deserve to be named once instead of branched on?
